title: Reverse Digits
question: Reverse digits of integer n.

solution.code:
def reverseDigits(n):
    sign = -1 if n < 0 else 1
    n = abs(n)
    rev = 0
    while n:
        rev = rev * 10 + n % 10
        n //= 10
    return sign * rev

title: N-Queens
question: Return all distinct n-queens solutions.

solution.code:
def solveNQueens(n):
    def backtrack(row):
        if row == n:
            res.append([''.join(r) for r in board])
            return
        for col in range(n):
            if col in cols or (row - col) in diag or (row + col) in anti:
                continue
            cols.add(col)
            diag.add(row - col)
            anti.add(row + col)
            board[row][col] = 'Q'
            backtrack(row + 1)
            board[row][col] = '.'
            cols.remove(col)
            diag.remove(row - col)
            anti.remove(row + col)
    res = []
    board = [['.'] * n for _ in range(n)]
    cols = diag = anti = set()
    backtrack(0)
    return res

explanation: Solve n-queens using an efficient approach.

title: Combination Sum
question: Return combinations summing to target.

solution.code:
def combinationSum(candidates, target):
    res = []
    def backtrack(i, cur, total):
        if total == target:
            res.append(cur[:])
            return
        if total > target or i == len(candidates):
            return
        cur.append(candidates[i])
        backtrack(i, cur, total + candidates[i])
        cur.pop()
        backtrack(i + 1, cur, total)
    backtrack(0, [], 0)
    return res

explanation: Solve combination sum using an efficient approach.

title: Maximum Product Subarray
question: Return max product subarray.

solution.code:
def maxProduct(nums):
    res = cur_max = cur_min = nums[0]
    for x in nums[1:]:
        candidates = (x, cur_max * x, cur_min * x)
        cur_max = max(candidates)
        cur_min = min(candidates)
        res = max(res, cur_max)
    return res

title: Merge Sort
question: Return sorted array using merge sort.

solution.code:
def mergeSort(arr):
    if len(arr) <= 1:
        return arr
    mid = len(arr) // 2
    left = mergeSort(arr[:mid])
    right = mergeSort(arr[mid:])
    i = j = 0
    res = []
    while i < len(left) and j < len(right):
        if left[i] <= right[j]:
            res.append(left[i])
            i += 1
        else:
            res.append(right[j])
            j += 1
    res.extend(left[i:])
    res.extend(right[j:])
    return res

explanation: Solve merge sort using an efficient approach.

title: Count Inversions
question: Return inversion count in array.

solution.code:
def countInversions(arr):
    def merge_sort_count(arr):
        if len(arr) <= 1:
            return arr, 0
        mid = len(arr) // 2
        left, inv_left = merge_sort_count(arr[:mid])
        right, inv_right = merge_sort_count(arr[mid:])
        merged = []
        i = j = inv = 0
        while i < len(left) and j < len(right):
            if left[i] <= right[j]:
                merged.append(left[i])
                i += 1
            else:
                merged.append(right[j])
                j += 1
                inv += len(left) - i
        merged.extend(left[i:])
        merged.extend(right[j:])
        return merged, inv_left + inv_right + inv
    _, inv = merge_sort_count(arr)
    return inv

explanation: Solve count inversions using an efficient approach.
hints: Consider the approach for count inversions.
